t: This was Browning Hall, properly the Robert Browning Settlement, set up in Walworth in 1895. It was one of the settlements that grew out of the settlement and university extension movements. It offered social services to the poor of a deprived area, and gave relatively well-educated people a place to live among the people they worked with. Its founder was the social reformer Francis Herbert Stead. He also served on the National Committee of Organised Labour, which campaigned for tax-funded old-age pensions from 1899.
